title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 28-30): Grothendieck is axiomatizing an abstract 'analysis situs' of stratified objects. Page 28 has replaced the structure (𝔉, ≤, ≪) by a set M with a family 𝔉_M ⊂ Fig(M) ⊂ 𝔓𝔓(M). Each element Φ of 𝔉_M is an 'ensemblist figure' in M, that is, a set of subsets ('strata') of M. He now restates the axioms (to become C1-C7) as Ax*1, Ax*2, ... in terms of the pair (M, 𝔉_M).

This page:
(1) He defines M* = ⋃_{Φ∈𝔉_M} Φ = {A ⊂ M | ∃Φ ∈ 𝔉_M with A ∈ Φ}, the set of all strata of all figures of 𝔉_M.
(2) Ax*1. M* is itself an ensemblist figure in M with support M. Moreover, the preorder this figure induces on M is a partial order. Concretely: for x ≠ y in M there is A ∈ M* containing exactly one of x and y. This is a T0 (Kolmogorov) separation condition.
(3) Consequence. Let ≪ be the associated order and set Omb(x) = M_{≪x} (the 'shadow' of x, its down-set). Then x ↦ Omb(x), M → 𝔓(M), induces a bijection M ≅ M* that carries ≪ to inclusion.
(4) In topological language: give M the Alexandrov-type topology whose closed sets are the ≪-down-sets. Then the strata A ∈ M* are exactly the closed irreducible subsets having a generic point, i.e. the point closures. The map x ↦ closure of x is injective precisely because the space is T0.
(5) He begins to deduce that every Φ ∈ 𝔉_M is a subset of M* ≅ M. The next page concludes that Φ = {Omb(x) | x ∈ F} for a unique F ⊂ M. So 𝔉_M is equivalently a family 𝔉̃ ⊂ 𝔓(M), subject to:
- preadmissibility: for each x there is a smallest member containing it;
- stability under unions bounded above in 𝔉_M.

Purpose: to reduce the axiomatics of 'figures' (the combinatorial skeleton of a stratified space: a poset of strata, plus admissible unions of strata) to a single poset M with a distinguished family of subsets.
errors: Minor redundancy: a closed set admitting a generic point is automatically irreducible, so 'irréductibles' is superfluous; the condition 'admettant un pt générique' is the essential one (needed for infinite posets, where irreducible down-sets need not be principal).

Implicit step: M* being a figure 'de support M' plus the T0 condition is what makes x ↦ Omb(x) land in M* and be surjective onto it. The page asserts the bijection without checking that every stratum A ∈ M* is of the form Omb(x); this presumably follows from the definition of 'figure ensembliste' given earlier in the chapter.

ideas.what: T0 condition on the preorder induced by strata, so that it is an order
Bijection of points with point-closures (shadows Omb(x)), carrying order to inclusion; strata = closed sets with a generic point
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology on a poset; generic points / sobriety-type correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. S. Alexandrov (1937); generic points in EGA

ideas.what: Encoding a stratified object by a poset of strata M together with a family of admissible subsets (figures)
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified spaces / stratifications as maps to posets with the Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A (2010s), with earlier roots (MacPherson, Treumann)
ideas.where_published: Spirit only in Esquisse d'un programme (tame topology, stratified structures); this formalism not published

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck reduces his abstract 'figure' axiomatics for analysis situs to a poset (M, ≪) carrying the Alexandrov topology, with strata identified to point closures. This prefigures the modern practice of treating stratifications as continuous maps to posets with the Alexandrov topology. It is a documented but unpublished instance of that viewpoint inside his tame-topology programme.
missed.quote: Les A ∈ M* sont les parties fermées irréductibles de M admettant un pt générique.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck's unpublished stratified-space foundations moving toward the poset-indexed framework later standard (Lurie, exit-path ∞-categories). The page itself contains only routine order/topology facts.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states routine facts: the T0 condition, specialization order, and points corresponding to point closures with generic points. Its interest lies only in its place within the unpublished stratified 'analysis situs' axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: 'figure assemblable[?]' is most likely 'figure ensembliste' (consistent with p.28's 'figures ensemblistes dans M').
The axiom label is written 'Ax*1' (resembling 'At*1'), consistent with p.28's 'Ax*1 etc.'.
'(soit Σ(ε)[?])' looks more like '(cond Σ(c))' or a similar condition label; uncertain.
In the last line, 'donc F ⊂ 𝒫(M)' should read 'donc Φ ⊂ 𝒫(M)' (bold Φ); the figure symbol is Φ throughout.
'Omb(x)' (ombre, shadow) is correct, defined as M_{≪x}.
